+## What
+Start phase 4 of eventplan.md (§ "Phases", "Phase 4 — mcp"). Add the wire library and the folder that the MCP capability lives in.
+
+- Modify `Package.swift`: add `.package(url: "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk.git", from: "0.12.1")` and the product `.product(name: "MCP", package: "swift-sdk")` to the library target and to the unit test target. +- Modify `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` if the nested package must resolve the new dependency to build (check with `swift build` in that folder).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `swift build` succeeds with `import MCP` in a file of the library target.
+- [ ] `swift build` in `IntegrationTests/` succeeds.
+- [ ] No `swift-log` dependency appears in `Package.swift`.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Extend `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/DependencyReachTests.swift`: add a test that `MCP.Tool` and `MCP.Client` are reachable from the test target (the same pattern the file uses for `Subprocess`).
+- [ ] `swift test --filter DependencyReachTests` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the reach test first, then add the dependency. #eventplan #phase-4

+Start phase 4 of eventplan.md (§ "Phases", "Phase 4 — mcp"). Add the wire library, the folder that the MCP capability lives in, and the dated note that records the phase-4 decisions — first, so the twenty tasks built on those decisions are built on an amended plan.

 - Modify `Package.swift`: add `.package(url: "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk.git", from: "0.12.1")` and the product `.product(name: "MCP", package: "swift-sdk")` to the library target and to the unit test target.  - Do NOT add `swift-log`. This package logs with `os.Logger` (see `MultiTool.swift`). Each ported MCP file uses `os.Logger` also.
 - Create `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/MCP/MCPCapability.swift` with a header comment only, in the `//` block style of `Capabilities/Shell/ShellCapability.swift`. +- **Amend `eventplan.md`.** Add a dated note (2026-08-27) under "Phase 4 — mcp", in ASD-STE100, with these decisions:
+  1. An MCP verb is a plain synchronous `Tool`. It does not conform to `BackgroundTool`, and no `RunKind` case is added. § "Consolidation of the siblings" lists "An MCP request (a protocol task)" as an object behind a parked run; that sentence now reads: an MCP request runs inside the run that called it; cancellation of that run becomes the advisory `notifications/cancelled` on the wire, and the outcome is the calling run's. A transport drop under an in-flight request throws a `LostRunError` (Router), and the engine settles the calling run as `.lost`. The reason is the content plane: an MCP result has no store, so a background envelope would give the model a 4 KB tail and nothing else.
+  2. The verbs of files, shell, and MCP are plain `FoundationModels.Tool` conformers that work on a bare `LanguageModelSession`. Background and non-blocking elicitation are what Router adds. On a bare session, MCP elicitation goes to a host handler on `MCPServer`, and the turn waits.
+  3. Router supplies the turn boundary through `TurnBoundaryTool.turnWillBegin()`; MultiTool stages a rebuilt registry and applies it there.
+  4. ACPAgent does not import FoundationModelsMCP (manifest comment only), so the "consumer moves first" step is a check and a comment edit.

 ## Acceptance Criteria
 - [ ] `swift build` succeeds with `import MCP` in a file of the library target.
 - [ ] `swift build` in `IntegrationTests/` succeeds.

 - [ ] Extend `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/DependencyReachTests.swift`: add a test that `MCP.Tool` and `MCP.Client` are reachable from the test target (the same pattern the file uses for `Subprocess`).
